  • The chocolate tech giant is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.
  • It has been revealed that the promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hershey’s is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day only to celebrate the theatrical release of its newly introduced movie, giving customers several ways to take advantage of the promotion.

The chocolate tech giant is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.

It has been revealed that the promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900. However, the process for claiming the discount varies depending on where customers shop.

The promotion will take place on Wednesday, November 25, with discounted chocolate bars available through Hershey’s Chocolate World, Walmart, and Amazon Grocery.

Customers visiting Hershey’s Chocolate World locations in Hershey, Pennsylvania, or Times Square in New York City can purchase the bars for five cents each beginning at 9 AM local time.

There is a limit of 10 bars per person, and the offer cannot be combined with other discounts. Applicable taxes will still be charged.

Walmart customers can also take advantage of the promotion through two different methods. Those shopping online can purchase a classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bar for five cents by placing an online pickup order through Walmart.com using their Walmart account.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, customers shopping at Walmart stores can receive the discounted price through the Ibotta app. After purchasing a qualifying chocolate bar, shoppers must upload a photo of their receipt to receive cash back.

Walmart’s promotion is limited to five bars per person and does not apply to orders shipped directly to customers’ homes.

Chipotle introduces hoodie designed to sneak burritos into movie theaters.

7 Brew adds food to its menu for the first time with five fresh $3 treats.

Reese’s adds bizarre warning to Halloween candy after $5 million lawsuit.

Amazon Grocery will also participate in the promotion, offering five-cent chocolate bars through same-day delivery in select markets.

Industry observers note that customers with qualifying delivery addresses can use a promotional code shared through Hershey’s social media channels to receive free shipping at checkout. The offer is limited to two bars per customer while supplies last, with taxes calculated based on the total order.

“The five-cent bar gives fans a chance to experience a sweet piece of Hershey’s story for themselves,” the company noted in a statement shared with PEOPLE.

“Bringing it back on the day HERSHEY debuts in theaters gives fans a fun way to celebrate the brand’s roots and the story that inspired it.”.

Alongside the promotion, Hershey’s is introducing vintage-inspired packaging for several products, including its Milk Chocolate Bars and Kisses chocolates.

The packaging features the firm’s historic wordmark, Milton Hershey’s signature, and typography inspired by the brand’s early years. Each package also includes a QR code directing customers to more information about Hershey’s history.

The upcoming movie stars Finn Wittrock as Milton Hershey and Alexandra Daddario as Catherine Hershey, following their relationship and the development of the chocolate company.

Directed by Mark Waters and filmed in Pennsylvania, the movie also features Alan Ruck, David Costabile, Richard Kind, and several other cast members.

A device disconnects halfway through a test. The application reports a timeout, the firmware restarts, and the next attempt succeeds. Where should you start?

For developers working with connected devices, browser interfaces, or hardware prototypes, an application error is often only the final symptom. Replacing code without recording the conditions around a failure can leave you chasing the wrong layer.

Industry observers note that this tutorial builds a small browser-based diagnostic log. It records measurements, preserves the test conditions, and exports evidence for another developer to review. You need basic HTML and JavaScript knowledge; no framework or connected instrument is required.

Industry observers note that 1. Define the question before collecting data Consider a hypothetical development board that disconnects when a peripheral starts. Several explanations remain possible: a firmware exception, a transport problem, or a power supply glitch. Start with a testable question: “Does the measured supply voltage change when this peripheral starts?” That question tells you what to record and what to keep constant.

Use a known-good board of the same revision where available. Match the firmware, cable, supply, peripheral, and workload. A comparison loses value when several conditions change together.

Record the observation separately from the explanation:.

The hypothesis remains provisional. A reading taken after the device restarts does not establish what happened during the failure.

It has been revealed that 2. Choose evidence that answers the question Application logs, firmware traces, and bench measurements answer different questions. A timeout establishes that an operation did not finish in time; it does not identify a failed component.

Recent findings suggest that for a view of specialist equipment used in phone-board troubleshooting, DIYFIXTOOL’s overview of Chip-Level Diagnostic Tools discusses thermal imaging, BGA X-ray inspection, and inductance testing. Treat it as a vendor-authored introduction to equipment categories; use instrument documentation and board-specific references when interpreting measurements.

The log below deliberately leaves interpretation to the operator. Enter a numeric value, its unit, and the conditions under which it was measured. Do not turn an isolated reading into an automatic “faulty chip” verdict.

For physical measurements, follow the board and instrument documentation and work within your training. This tutorial covers the software record rather than a procedure for probing or repairing a powered device. 3. Build a small, accessible form.

Recent findings suggest that save the following as index.html and serve it through your usual local development server. For example, if Python is installed, run python -m http. server 8000 in its directory, then open http://localhost:8000. 4. Preserve data without hiding failures.

The application stores an array of records as JSON. On reload, it parses that JSON and checks the expected field types before rendering it. Parsing alone does not validate the structure of stored data.

Recent findings suggest that sitePoint’s guide to looping through JSON responses provides useful background on working with objects and arrays after parsing JSON. Each table cell uses textContent, so a note containing HTML is displayed as text rather than inserted as markup. The MDN documentation for textContent explains this behavior.

Storage operations sit inside try...catch blocks because browser persistence can fail. The interface keeps new measurements in memory and offers an export when saving fails. It does not claim those measurements will survive a reload. For another practical vanilla JavaScript project, SitePoint’s **Markdown previewer tutorial **explores browser UI construction and persistence.

It has been revealed that as **MDN’s localStorage documentation **explains, storage belongs to the document’s origin. Opening the application on a different port may therefore show a different log. This prototype is a single-browser tool, so export important sessions and avoid recording customer identifiers or private device contents.

5. Compare measurements under matching conditions Suppose two hypothetical readings are 3.29 V and 3.08 V. Their difference is −0.21 V. That arithmetic is straightforward; its meaning depends on the rail specification, measurement uncertainty, workload, and timing.

Do not add a universal voltage threshold to the application. A device-specific limit should come from its specification or an established test procedure.

In a recent development, if the failure is brief, a manually entered steady-state measurement may miss it entirely. Record that limitation. The next investigation may require a time-correlated capture rather than another static reading.

When sharing a session, include the firmware revision, board revision, instrument settings, and reproduction steps. A colleague should be able to repeat the comparison without guessing how the reading was obtained. 6. Verify the workflow before relying on it Try adding a decimal reading and a negative reading, then reload the page. Confirm that both values and their units remain intact. Enter a note containing test and check that it appears literally in the table.

In a recent development, export the JSON and inspect the record count. Then simulate blocked storage and confirm that the interface reports the failure while allowing an export of the current session.

Sources indicate that for a larger application, add editable entries, instrument metadata, and explicit baseline records. A shared service would also need access controls, server-side validation, and a policy for retention. These additions should follow the needs of the diagnostic workflow.

Turn a symptom into a reproducible investigation.

It has been revealed that the finished prototype captures a useful minimum: what was measured, where, when, and under which conditions. Its value comes from preserving evidence that another person can inspect.

When an application error crosses into firmware or hardware, that record helps you choose the next experiment. Repeat the failure, change one variable, and document what the latest evidence supports before deciding what to fix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has cut longtime ways to hook up with other characters in GTA 6, including hiring sex workers, as it builds the game’s romance around Jason and Lucia.

GTA 3 let players pay for sex back in 2001, and later games gave them more ways to pursue other characters. San Andreas gave CJ six potential girlfriends, while GTA 4 let Niko Bellic meet dates through the in-game internet.

GTA 5 kept paid hookups and gave players another option at the Vanilla Unicorn strip club. Flirting with certain dancers during a private dance could lead to leaving the club with them, hooking up, and calling them again later.

GTA 6 still puts Jason in suggestive situations in the main story with side characters attempting to seduce him, and strangers around Leonida flirt with him openly and invite him into explicit situations. But unlike GTA games from before, that’s as intimate as Jason is allowed to get.

Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said a trip to the strip club was the closest he found to a way to cheat on Lucia, and he later confirmed you cannot kiss anyone except your partner.

You can't kiss anyone except your partner.

The Guardian’s review confirmed that either lead can get a private dance on their own or the couple can go together. Shacknews confirmed that players can no longer pick up sex workers.

According to recent reports, rockstar described Jason and Lucia as “a couple in a bind, lovers on the run” in a statement to Shacknews. The studio said it chose which features to bring forward based on how they fit the story and the gameplay systems it wanted to expand.

GTA 6 is giving players more freedom to complete missions their own way.

GTA 6 almost had four playable characters instead of just Jason and Lucia.

GTA 6 confirms realistic NPCs, deeper relationships, body changes, social media system & more.

“While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story… Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story.”.

GTA 6 gives players several ways to build intimacy between the two leads. Jason and Lucia can go dancing, hold hands, and make each other coffee. The couple can also become more affectionate and intimate when the relationship is going well.

Industry observers note that how romantic that partnership becomes is up to the player. Rockstar development head Rob Nelson has mentioned players can let the romance cool while Jason and Lucia continue to work together as the story unfolds.

  • Myers, 43, pleaded guilty in July 2025 to felony stalking and harassment charges involving Shannon Walker, the wife of Tucson city prosecutor Matthew Walker.
  • In October 2026, Pima County Superior Court Judge Douglas Metcalf sentenced Myers to three years in prison for violating that probation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Arizona judge ordered YouTuber Lane Myers released from prison after county prosecutors raised doubts about an email that helped send him there.

Myers, 43, pleaded guilty in July 2025 to felony stalking and harassment charges involving Shannon Walker, the wife of Tucson city prosecutor Matthew Walker. He was placed on probation under conditions that restricted what he could post about the couple.

In October 2026, Pima County Superior Court Judge Douglas Metcalf sentenced Myers to three years in prison for violating that probation. Prosecutors remarked Myers had posted fresh YouTube videos about the Walkers and argued those videos prompted others to send Shannon Walker threatening and harassing emails.

Investigators tied at least one of those emails to an IP address associated with the Walkers’ home, casting doubt on whether the message came from someone reacting to Myers’ videos. Who sent it remains under investigation.

Deputy County Attorney Rachel Stiles submitted the latest evidence under seal and discussed it only in broad terms at the November 17 hearing.

In a recent development, tucson police searched the Walkers’ home on November 2 and seized several devices, including Matthew Walker’s city-issued laptop. County prosecutors first asked for Myers’ release at an emergency hearing the next day. On November 5, the city of Tucson put Matthew Walker on paid administrative leave while police investigated possible misconduct connected to the probation case.

A Tucson YouTuber was ordered freed from prison after county prosecutors found evidence suggesting the victim or her husband, a city prosecutor, may have drafted harassing emails that helped put him behind bars. https://t.co/An6DVVsuFD.

Industry observers note that metcalf returned Myers to probation on November 17, and his 2025 stalking and harassment convictions still stand. Myers thanked county prosecutors in a statement for bringing the evidence forward, and thanked Metcalf for “giving me the opportunity to show I can follow conditions.”.

Stiles mentioned county prosecutors still believe Myers violated his probation and will review the evidence before deciding whether to ask the court to revoke it again. Metcalf scheduled a status hearing for December 8.

Think about what's sitting in your inbox and Drive right now. Client contracts and invoices. Project specs under NDA. Staging credentials a client emailed you. That API key or password you meant to delete.

For most developers and freelancers, all of it lives in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365. Both are excellent tools, and both encrypt your data in transit and at rest. But in their standard setup, the provider holds the encryption keys, which means your provider (and the integrated apps and AI features connected to it) can access what's inside.

Proton Workspace takes a different approach: the same everyday tools, with encryption designed so that not even Proton can read your data.

Here's how the three compare, what each does best, and which makes the most sense for how you work.

Google and Microsoft are built around ecosystem integration. Proton is built around keeping your data yours, without sacrificing productivity tools.

Sources indicate that google Workspace is the go-to suite for startups, agencies and freelancers, and for good reason. Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar and Meet work together seamlessly, and several people can edit the same file in real time without emailing versions back and forth.

In a recent development, google encrypts data at rest and in transit, and offers client-side encryption on eligible editions. But that extra layer requires higher-tier plans and configuration, so in the default experience Google holds the keys. A password manager and VPN aren't part of the suite.

Best for: Teams whose top priorities are real-time collaboration and third-party integrations.

In a recent development, if your work runs on Word, Excel and Outlook, Microsoft 365 needs little introduction. Business Standard includes full desktop apps, and Excel remains the benchmark for heavy spreadsheet work.

Industry observers note that that breadth comes with complexity. Licensing, permissions and device management can eat into time a small team or solo developer would rather spend shipping. And like Google, Microsoft's everyday productivity experience isn't built around end-to-end encryption, while Copilot and advanced security features add cost.

Best for: Businesses built on desktop Office apps and established Microsoft workflows.

Proton Workspace starts from a different premise. Instead of building a productivity suite and adding privacy features on top, Proton built privacy into the foundation, then delivered the everyday tools around it.

What's included in Workspace Standard:.

Everything is managed from one admin console, with one bill.

This is the core difference. Proton uses zero-access encryption: your data is encrypted before it reaches Proton's servers, and Proton never holds the keys. Proton can't read your data. Not won't. Can't.

That has practical consequences:.

Industry observers note that the honest trade-offs: Proton Docs and Sheets cover core editing and collaboration, not every advanced Excel feature. There's no presentation app yet, and the third-party integration ecosystem is smaller than Google's or Microsoft's.

Best for: Developers, freelancers, agencies and startups that handle client data, code and credentials, and want privacy and savings in one suite.

US prices for comparable plans with annual billing, excluding taxes:.

In a recent development, the headline prices are close. The real cost isn't:.

Industry observers note that proton Workspace covers business email, 1 TB of encrypted storage, docs, sheets, video calls, a password manager and a VPN. That's one bill instead of three.

According to recent reports, need more? Workspace Premium and adds 3 TB of storage per user, 20 custom domains, meetings for up to 250 participants, Lumo private AI and email data retention policies for only $7 more per month. Both looks include a 14-day free trial, and annual plans are right now up to 20% off.

Choose Google Workspace if your team lives in real-time collaboration and relies heavily on Google's integration ecosystem.

Choose Microsoft 365 if your work depends on desktop Excel, PowerPoint and established Microsoft workflows.

Choose Proton Workspace if you handle client data, proprietary code or credentials you don't want readable by your provider or if you want privacy you can verify, with open-source, audited apps.

It has been revealed that less than you might expect. Proton's Easy Switch tool imports email, contacts and calendars from Google Workspace and other providers, and you keep your custom domain, so clients won't notice a thing. Smaller teams can migrate on their own, and Proton's business team supports larger moves.

Moving from Microsoft 365? Check the migration options for each data type rather than assuming every workflow transfers automatically.

Is Proton Workspace a good alternative to Google Workspace for developers?

Yes, for developers who prioritize privacy and cost. It covers email, storage, documents, spreadsheets and video calls, adds a password manager and VPN, and costs $12.99/user/month versus $14 for Google Workspace Business Standard.

Can Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 read my email and files?

Sources indicate that by default, yes. Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 hold the encryption keys, and their default terms give them access to your data.

Can Proton read my email and files?

No. Zero-access encryption means Proton never holds the keys to your stored data. Emails between Proton users are end-to-end encrypted automatically, and you can send password-protected encrypted emails to anyone.

In a recent development, yes. Proton's apps are open source and independently audited.

Can I use Proton Mail with my existing email client?

Recent findings suggest that yes. Proton Mail Bridge connects Outlook, Apple Mail and Thunderbird.

Does Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 use my data to train AI?

It can. If your plan allows Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 to hold the encryption keys, they can access your data and use it to train their integrated AI models.

Does Proton use my data to train AI?

No. Proton can't read your data, so it can't use it for AI training.

Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 are mature, capable platforms, and if your work depends on advanced Excel or a deep web of Google integrations, there's a good case for using them.

The newly introduced creation, called the HeartWhopper, is part of a limited-time promotion from Burger King Belgium that allows GTA fans to win a real version of the oversized burger.

The campaign debuts on November 19 and takes inspiration from the fictional fast-food chain found throughout the GTA series, turning one of its recognizable menu items into an actual meal.

The HeartWhopper features seven flame-grilled beef patties stacked with cheese, tomato slices, lettuce, and onion rings, recreating the exaggerated burgers associated with the fictional restaurant.

According to Burger King, the promotion is intended as a parody of the video game franchise’s own parody of fast-food chains, with the company claiming its restaurants have served as inspiration for fictional businesses in gaming.

Rather than introducing the HeartWhopper as a traditional menu item, Burger King Belgium is giving players the chance to win one through a social media competition.

A post shared by Burger King BE & LUX (@burgerkingbe).

To participate, fans must share a video clip showing themselves enjoying a burger from the in-game restaurant and tag either Burger King Belgium or Burger King Luxembourg.

The manufacturer will select the most creative submission each day, awarding the winner a real-life HeartWhopper. The competition will run for two weeks, giving players multiple opportunities to participate.

Burger King is also promoting the campaign through YouTube advertisements, YouTube Shorts, and gaming communities on Reddit, with teasers released ahead of the November 19 launch.

Scientists built the hardest AI test ever and the results are surprising

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as artificial intelligence systems began scoring extremely high on long used academic benchmarks, researchers noticed a growing matter.
  • To solve this problem, a worldwide group of nearly 1,000 researchers, including a professor from Texas A&M University, developed a newly introduced type of test.
  • According to recent reports, the result is "Humanity's Last Exam" (HLE), a 2,500 question assessment covering mathematics, humanities, natural sciences, ancient languages, and a wide range of highly specialized academic fields.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as artificial intelligence systems began scoring extremely high on long used academic benchmarks, researchers noticed a growing matter. The tests that once challenged machines were no longer difficult enough. Well known evaluations such as the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) exam, which had previously been seen as demanding, now fail to properly measure the capabilities of today's advanced AI models.

To solve this problem, a worldwide group of nearly 1,000 researchers, including a professor from Texas A&M University, developed a newly introduced type of test. Their goal was to build an exam that is broad, difficult, and grounded in expert human knowledge in ways that current AI systems still struggle to handle.

According to recent reports, the result is "Humanity's Last Exam" (HLE), a 2,500 question assessment covering mathematics, humanities, natural sciences, ancient languages, and a wide range of highly specialized academic fields. Details of the project appear in a paper published in Nature, and additional information about the exam is available at lastexam.ai.

Recent findings suggest that among the many contributors is Dr. Tung Nguyen, instructional associate professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Texas A&M. Nguyen helped write and refine many of the exam questions.

"When AI systems start performing extremely well on human benchmarks, it's tempting to think they're approaching human-level understanding," Nguyen noted. "But HLE reminds us that intelligence isn't just about pattern recognition -- it's about depth, context and specialized expertise.".

The purpose of the exam was not to trick or defeat human test takers. Instead, the goal was to carefully identify areas where AI systems still fall short.

A Global Effort to Measure AI's Limits.

In a recent development, specialists from around the world wrote and reviewed the questions included in Humanity's Last Exam. Each problem was carefully designed so it has one clear, verifiable answer. The questions were also crafted to prevent quick solutions through simple internet searches.

The topics come from advanced academic challenges. Some tasks involve translating ancient Palmyrene inscriptions, while others require identifying tiny anatomical structures in birds or analyzing detailed features of Biblical Hebrew pronunciation.

Researchers tested every question against leading AI systems. If any model was able to answer a question correctly, that question was removed from the final exam. This process ensured the test remained just beyond what current AI systems can reliably solve.

According to recent reports, early testing confirmed that the strategy worked. Even powerful AI models struggled with the exam. GPT-4o achieved a score of 2.7 percent, while Claude 3.5 Sonnet reached 4.1 percent. OpenAI's o1 model performed somewhat better with 8 percent. The most capable systems so far, including Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6, have reached accuracy levels between about 40 percent and 50 percent.

Why New AI Benchmarks Are Needed.

Nguyen explained that the issue of AI surpassing older tests is more than a technical concern. He contributed 73 of the 2,500 publicly available questions in HLE, the second highest number among contributors, and wrote the most questions related to mathematics and computer science.

In a recent development, "Without accurate assessment tools, policymakers, developers and owners risk misinterpreting what AI systems can actually do," he said. "Benchmarks provide the foundation for measuring progress and identifying risks.".

It has been revealed that according to the research team, high scores on tests originally designed for humans do not necessarily indicate genuine intelligence. Those benchmarks mainly measure how well AI can complete specific tasks created for human learners, rather than capturing deeper understanding.

In a recent development, despite the dramatic name, Humanity's Last Exam is not meant to suggest that humans are becoming obsolete. Instead, it highlights the large amount of knowledge and expertise that still remains uniquely human.

"This isn't a race against AI," Nguyen remarked. "It's a method for understanding where these systems are strong and where they struggle. That understanding helps us build safer, more reliable technologies. And, importantly, it reminds us why human expertise still matters.".

Building a Long Term AI Benchmark.

Humanity's Last Exam is designed to serve as a durable and transparent benchmark for future AI systems. To support that goal, the researchers have released some questions publicly while keeping the majority hidden so that AI models cannot simply memorize the answers.

"For now, Humanity's Last Exam stands as one of the clearest assessments of the gap between AI and human intelligence," Nguyen said, "and despite rapid technological advances, it remains wide.".

A Massive International Research Effort.

Nguyen emphasized that the scale of the project demonstrates the value of collaboration across disciplines and countries.

"What made this project extraordinary was the scale," he mentioned. "Experts from nearly every discipline contributed. It wasn't just computer scientists; it was historians, physicists, linguists, medical researchers. That diversity is exactly what exposes the gaps in today's AI systems -- perhaps ironically, it's humans working together.".

Scientists discover AI can make humans more creative

📅 16 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence (AI) is commonly viewed as a technology designed to automate work and potentially replace human labor.
  • Sources indicate that researchers from the University's Computer Science Department carried out one of the largest studies so far examining how people work alongside AI during creative design tasks.
  • Recent findings suggest that rather than quietly optimizing designs behind the scenes, the system used a method called MAP-Elites to produce visual galleries filled with many different design possibilities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence (AI) is commonly viewed as a technology designed to automate work and potentially replace human labor. However, latest research from Swansea University offers a different perspective. The findings suggest that AI can also function as a creative collaborator that encourages exploration, engagement, and inspiration.

Sources indicate that researchers from the University's Computer Science Department carried out one of the largest studies so far examining how people work alongside AI during creative design tasks. More than 800 participants joined an online experiment where they used an AI-supported system to design virtual cars.

How AI Generated Diverse Design Ideas.

Recent findings suggest that rather than quietly optimizing designs behind the scenes, the system used a method called MAP-Elites to produce visual galleries filled with many different design possibilities. These galleries demonstrated a wide spectrum of car concepts, including highly effective designs, unusual ideas, and even some intentionally flawed options.

Turing Fellow Dr. Sean Walton, Associate Professor of Computer Science and the study's lead author, explained: "People often think of AI as something that speeds up tasks or improves efficiency, but our findings suggest something far more interesting. When people were shown AI-generated design suggestions, they spent more time on the task, produced better designs and felt more involved. It was not just about efficiency. It was about creativity and collaboration.".

Why Traditional AI Evaluation May Be Too Limited.

Sources indicate that the study, published in the ACM journal Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems, also highlights a problem with how AI design tools are typically assessed. Standard metrics often focus on simple behaviors, such as how frequently owners click on or copy AI suggestions. According to the researchers, these measures overlook important aspects of the experience, including how the technology influences people's thoughts, emotions, and willingness to explore latest ideas.

It has been revealed that the Swansea researchers argue that AI systems should be evaluated using broader methods that capture these deeper effects. Understanding how AI shapes human thinking and engagement could provide a more complete picture of its impact.

Why Imperfect Ideas Can Boost Creativity.

Dr. Walton emphasized that variety in AI-generated output played a crucial role in the experiment. "Our study highlights the importance of diversity in AI output. Participants responded most positively to galleries that included a wide variety of ideas, including bad ones! These helped them move beyond their initial assumptions and explore a broader design space. This structured diversity prevented early fixation and encouraged creative risk-taking.

"As AI becomes increasingly embedded in creative fields, from engineering and architecture to music and game design, understanding how humans and intelligent systems work together is essential. As the technology evolves, the question is not only what AI can do but how it can help us think, create and collaborate more effectively.".

Japan is no stranger when it comes to censoring video games, with recent examples like Resident Evil Requiem famously featuring black textures over decapitated body parts and less blood.

However, on November 10, it was revealed that the Japanese version of GTA 6 was 1 GB smaller than its overseas brother. This swiftly sparked fears among players that the game would be missing content to make it pass Japan’s ratings board. Well, it turns out that those fears were indeed true.

Recent findings suggest that A screenshot of protagonist Jason taking a shower in the Japanese version of the game has gone viral, and no, it’s not because he’s getting all soapy. Rather, it’s because he’s showering in what can only be described as a tiny black Speedo.

It has been revealed that for contrast, the overseas release has Jason showering in his birthday suit, with there being no steam or swimwear to obstruct his bare buttocks from view. As you can imagine, many fans aren’t exactly happy with these watered-down scenes.

“Isn’t it strange that in a country where people go completely naked in public baths and hot springs, they make people wear swimsuits to take a shower?” wrote one Japanese player.

“If they’re going out of their way to give it a CERO Z rating for 18+, what’s the point of censoring the content? I don’t get it,” replied another commenter.

“They could just use parental controls and the like to restrict content that’s harmful to children, but instead, decent adults get content shoved at them that’s been watered down to the point of having its teeth pulled,” added another angry fan.

Sources indicate that every prompt registry we tested can change a prompt in a running TypeScript app, roll it back, and give production and staging different versions. LangSmith's prompt hub, Langfuse, Phoenix and AcruxCore all passed those three tests. The real differences show up elsewhere: which template syntax each one accepts, how many npm packages it pulls in, how long a change takes to reach the app, and what happens when the registry is down.

We tested all of this with one small app and one prompt, which has a condition and a loop. Git files served as the baseline. Every number below comes from a recorded run.

Most teams start with prompts in code: a template string, or a .txt file next to the code that uses it. That works until a product manager wants to change one sentence, and the change has to wait for a full release.

According to recent reports, A prompt registry moves the text out of the deploy. The app fetches the prompt by name and by a label such as production. You change which version the label points to, and the app picks up the newly introduced text without a deploy.

Sources indicate that langSmith's prompt hub is the best-known registry, but it is not the only one. Several of the LangSmith alternatives also manage prompts, and three of them are open source and self-hostable: Langfuse, Phoenix and AcruxCore. We covered how those tools handle tracing in Self-Hosted LangSmith Alternatives: 4 Tools Tested on One TypeScript Agent. This article covers prompts only.

It has been revealed that every tool got the same prompt, support-reply. Its template takes three variables: a customer name, a initiative, and a list of help articles. It has one condition: a priority line appears only for premium customers. It also has one loop: one line per help article. In Jinja2 syntax, the template looks like this:.

One help article contains the text Settings > Export. We included it on purpose, to catch any tool that HTML-escapes > into >.

Every tool then ran the same sequence from a TypeScript script:.

Each tool used its own documented TypeScript SDK. The four registries passed all six steps. The rest of this article covers how each one got there, and what it cost.

In a recent development, keeping prompts in the repository costs almost nothing. The template sits in prompts/support-reply.njk, and nunjucks, the JavaScript port of Jinja2, renders it:.

The autoescape: false line matters. Our first version called nunjucks.renderString() directly, and the test failed. The default environment HTML-escapes its output, so Settings > Export reached the model as Settings > Export. Escaping is correct for web pages and wrong for prompts.

It has been revealed that git gives you full Jinja2, code review on every prompt change, and history in the same place as the code. What it can't do is change a prompt in a running app. Every edit, and every rollback, waits for a deploy.

LangSmith stores a prompt as a serialized LangChain object (ChatPromptTemplate), not as plain text. LangSmith's own documentation says you must use the LangChain npm package to pull prompts in TypeScript (Manage prompts programmatically). So a plain TypeScript app that uses the openai package still needs langchain and @langchain/core:.

According to recent reports, those three packages installed 23 packages and 70 MB. Most of the size is @langchain/* (27 MB) and js-tiktoken (22 MB).

Templates. In TypeScript, LangChain accepts f-string and mustache templates. Mustache sections ({{#docs}}…{{/docs}}) handled our loop. Mustache has no ==, though, so the premium check became an is_premium boolean computed in code. We also tried templateFormat: "jinja2", which LangChain's Python package supports. In TypeScript it threw DEFAULT_PARSER_MAPPING[templateFormat] is not a function.

Industry observers note that labels and rollback. production and staging are reserved tags, and the documentation moves them in the UI. The langsmith JavaScript client has no public method that moves a tag. Our script called the same REST route the SDK uses internally (POST /api/v1/repos/-//tags). It worked, but it is not a documented API.

Sources indicate that caching. The SDK caches prompts for 300 seconds by default. In our test, a running app saw the fresh version 300 seconds after we moved the tag.

Langfuse's TypeScript client is one package, @langfuse/client. It installed 5 packages and 8 MB:.

Creating a version, moving a label and reading by label are all public SDK calls: prompt.create, prompt.update and prompt.get (Get started with prompt management).

It has been revealed that templates. The documentation shows only {{variable}} substitution. But compile() calls the mustache library, so sections worked for our loop. The type signature accepts only string values, so passing a list needed a cast. The Langfuse UI colours the section tags red, and it lists title and body as the prompt's variables, not docs or is_premium. We would not depend on behaviour the documentation doesn't promise. When we sent the Jinja2 version instead, Langfuse returned the {% if %} and {% for %} tags unchanged, with no error. The model would have received them as text.

Caching. The cache time is 60 seconds by default (Caching). Our app saw the change after 62 seconds. Langfuse is also the only client with a fallback option: a prompt string the SDK uses when it cannot reach the server on a cold start.

Phoenix's TypeScript client fetches a prompt by name and tag, and toSDK() converts it into the message format the openai package expects. Phoenix templates only replace variables, so the condition and the loop have to run in your code before rendering:.

It has been revealed that that is 16 lines, against 6 to 8 for the other registries. All the extra lines are template logic that now lives in the app.

In a recent development, templates. Phoenix offers MUSTACHE, F_STRING and NONE formats (Prompts reference). Even in MUSTACHE mode, though, rendering is a plain replacement of {{name}}. When we sent mustache sections, they came back unchanged, with no error.

Recent findings suggest that errors. getPrompt() catches every error, logs it and returns null. You can see this in the client source, src/utils/getPromptBySelector.ts. A missing prompt and an unreachable server look the same to your code, which is why the snippet checks for null.

Sources indicate that size and caching. The client installed 57 packages and 90 MB. Most of that is OpenTelemetry, which comes in through its @arizeai/phoenix-otel dependency. The client has no prompt cache, so every render is a network call. That is also why a label change indicated up immediately: 0 seconds in our test.

Recent findings suggest that acruxCore stores Jinja2 templates and renders them on the server with nunjucks. The SDK sends the variables and gets back finished messages:.

The template from the test section works as it is, condition and loop included, with no is_premium flag computed in code. A label is called an alias here, and promoteAlias() moves it (Manage prompts via the SDK). The SDK installed 3 packages and 12 MB. Most of the 12 MB is one OpenTelemetry package, @opentelemetry/semantic-conventions.

Industry observers note that templates. Jinja2 only. When we committed the mustache version, AcruxCore rejected it at commit time with Template parse error: unexpected token: #. That is a clear error, but it also means that moving mustache prompts from LangSmith or Langfuse requires rewriting them.

We sent the same two templates, a Jinja2 one and a mustache one, to each tool's own renderer:.

In a recent development, the rows that matter most are the ones where the tags were left in the output, because those failures produce no error. The model receives raw template syntax, and the only symptom is a strange answer. Whatever tool you pick, test one prompt with logic in it before you move the rest.

Recent findings suggest that putting logic in the template is not automatically better. It lets someone change the condition without a deploy. It also lets them break the condition without a deploy. Keeping logic in code, as Phoenix forces you to do, puts every branch under code review and in your tests.

A registry is a upcoming runtime dependency, so we tested an outage. The app reached each registry through a local proxy, and we switched the proxy off. A separate process then started while the registry was still unreachable.

LangSmith, Langfuse and AcruxCore keep serving the last good version while the registry is down, even after the cache time has passed. The risk is a cold start: a upcoming container or a serverless function that boots during the outage. Langfuse's fallback option is the built-in answer to that. With the other tools, keep a copy of each prompt in your code as a fallback, which brings back part of the Git setup.

Keep prompts in Git if engineers make every prompt change and your deploys are quick. Set autoescape: false, and you get Jinja2, reviews and history for free.

Sources indicate that use LangSmith's prompt hub if you already use LangChain, or already trace with LangSmith. If your app doesn't use LangChain, budget for the extra dependency and for the tag moves that only the UI supports.

Use Langfuse if you want a small client, a local compile(), and a fallback for cold starts. Keep to {{variable}} substitution unless you are comfortable relying on mustache behaviour that the documentation doesn't promise.

It has been revealed that use Phoenix if you already use it for tracing, or if you prefer all template logic in code. Remember the null check, and that every render is a network call.

According to recent reports, use AcruxCore if you want real conditions and loops in the template and rendering on the server. Expect one network call per new set of variables, and a personal API key for writes.

Before you choose, run one of your own prompts with real logic in it through the tool's SDK, not through its playground. Two of the four registries we tested failed on template syntax without any error, and an SDK run is where you would see that.

  • Over the last few years, a number of places have updated their security systems, scrapping old metal detectors in favor of newer ones – you’ll have seen them at airports, for example.
  • That has been the case for the Hempfield Area High School in Pennsylvania, as they have been helping to test the new Wi-AI detection system from CurvePoint AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A high school in Pennsylvania has been forced to scrap a test of AI-powered metal detectors after regular student items were continually flagged as weapons.

Over the last few years, a number of places have updated their security systems, scrapping old metal detectors in favor of newer ones – you’ll have seen them at airports, for example. These up-to-date detectors are supposed to speed up the security process, but they can cause headaches.

That has been the case for the Hempfield Area High School in Pennsylvania, as they have been helping to test the new Wi-AI detection system from CurvePoint AI.

As per TechSpot, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons, with people having to walk near SensePods, which tracks movements without even using cameras.

However, according to WTAE-TV in Pittsburgh, everyday items that students need for school – including binders, water bottles, and batteries – have been routinely flagged as weapons.

“The detection is not what they were hoping to get from the technology side of things and so, we are in agreement that, moving forward, as far as going live, its just not a product that is ready for that activation,” Superintendent Dr. Mark Holtzman told the news outlet.

Skip Smith, the CEO of CurvePoint AI, noted that the school “served as a testing and evaluation site” rather than being a full “operational deployment.”.

Additionally, Holtzman noted that the system was “not near” the 95% accuracy rate that the system hoped to achieve.

It isn’t the first time that similar systems have caused these sorts of headaches. Back in October 2025, a 16-year-old student in Baltimore was swarmed by armed police when an AI gun detection system falsely flagged a Doritos bag as a firearm. That system was shut down just a month later, too.

AI-powered robot learns how to harvest tomatoes more efficiently

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Farm labor shortages are pushing agriculture toward greater automation, especially when it comes to harvesting.
  • To tackle this challenge, Assistant Professor Takuya Fujinaga of Osaka Metropolitan University's Graduate School of Engineering developed a system that trains robots to assess how easy each tomato is to harvest before attempting to pick it.
  • It has been revealed that his approach combines image recognition with statistical analysis to determine the best angle for picking each fruit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Farm labor shortages are pushing agriculture toward greater automation, especially when it comes to harvesting. But not all crops are easy for machines to handle. Tomatoes, for example, grow in clusters, which means a robot must carefully select ripe fruit while leaving unripe ones untouched. This requires precise control and smart decision-making.

To tackle this challenge, Assistant Professor Takuya Fujinaga of Osaka Metropolitan University's Graduate School of Engineering developed a system that trains robots to assess how easy each tomato is to harvest before attempting to pick it.

It has been revealed that his approach combines image recognition with statistical analysis to determine the best angle for picking each fruit. The robot analyzes visual details such as the tomato itself, its stems, and whether it is hidden behind leaves or other parts of the plant. These inputs guide the robot in choosing the most effective way to approach and pick the fruit.

From Detection to "Harvest-Ease" Decision-Making.

Recent findings suggest that this method shifts away from traditional systems that focus only on detecting and identifying fruit. Instead, Fujinaga introduces what he calls "harvest-ease estimation." "This moves beyond simply asking 'can a robot pick a tomato?' to thinking about 'how likely is a successful pick?', which is more meaningful for real-world farming," he explained.

Recent findings suggest that in testing, the system achieved an 81% success rate, exceeding expectations. About one-quarter of the successful picks came from tomatoes that were harvested from the side after an initial front-facing attempt failed. This indicates the robot can adjust its approach when the first attempt is not successful.

The research underscores how many variables affect robotic harvesting, including how tomatoes cluster, the shape and position of stems, surrounding leaves, and visual obstruction. "This research establishes 'ease of harvesting' as a quantitatively evaluable metric, bringing us one step closer to the realization of agricultural robots that can make informed decisions and act intelligently," Fujinaga said.

Future of Human-Robot Collaboration in Farming.

It has been revealed that looking ahead, Fujinaga envisions robots that can independently judge when crops are ready to be picked. "This is expected to usher in a new form of agriculture where robots and humans collaborate," he explained. "Robots will automatically harvest tomatoes that are easy to pick, while humans will handle the more challenging fruits.".

The findings were published in Smart Agricultural Technology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Rockstar Games developer notes he and his colleagues are worried about losing their jobs after GTA 6, despite the successful launch.

The long-awaited sequel arrived on November 19 to rave reviews, after racking up well over $1 billion in pre-orders, and is likely to be one of, if not the biggest, video game releases ever.

GTA 5 sold more than 230 million copies, and Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte claims the follow-up is expected to surpass it.

But for some of the people who made it, launch week also brings questions about what happens in the weeks and months that follow.

It has been revealed that uriarte, who works at Rockstar’s Edinburgh studio, raised those concerns in an opinion piece for The Guardian. He described the pressure game developers have come to expect on either side of a major launch.

“While the highs of a game release like this can be incredible, game workers have also come to expect other, less welcome side effects: intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath,” Uriarte wrote.

He pointed to job losses across the games industry to explain why those fears persist, even at Rockstar.

“It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”.

As a result, Uriarte stated he was voting in favor of union recognition because he wants staff to have a say in pay, bonuses, and working conditions. He said Rockstar has already introduced some overtime pay and wants to build on that so workers are paid for every hour they put in.

He went on to admit that there has been no suggestion from Rockstar that layoffs are imminent, but that the fears are still there among staff.

“After the substantial day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds,” he added.

DNA robots could deliver drugs and hunt viruses inside your body

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine tiny robots made from DNA moving through the bloodstream, delivering drugs exactly where they are needed and targeting threats such as cancer cells or viruses.
  • Researchers are exploring how DNA can be engineered into working machines using creative design approaches.
  • It has been revealed that guiding the motion of DNA robots in a constantly shifting molecular environment is a major challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine tiny robots made from DNA moving through the bloodstream, delivering drugs exactly where they are needed and targeting threats such as cancer cells or viruses. These microscopic machines could also assemble ultra-precise data storage systems and computing devices at the nanometer scale. Although the possibilities are remarkable, most DNA robots today remain in early experimental stages and are better understood as proof of concept rather than practical tools.

Researchers are exploring how DNA can be engineered into working machines using creative design approaches. These include building rigid DNA joints, incorporating flexible components, and using folding techniques inspired by origami. By applying principles from larger-scale robotics such as rigid, compliant and origami robots, scientists are adapting familiar mechanical concepts to the nanoscale. This allows DNA-based systems to carry out controlled and repeatable tasks despite their extremely small size.

Controlling Movement in DNA Nanorobots.

It has been revealed that guiding the motion of DNA robots in a constantly shifting molecular environment is a major challenge. To address this, scientists have developed control systems that help these machines behave in predictable ways. One crucial method involves DNA strand displacement, a biochemical process that enables precise programming of movement using specific DNA sequences labeled as "fuel" and "structure.".

It has been revealed that in addition to biochemical control, external physical signals such as electric fields, magnetic fields, and light can direct how these robots move. Together, these approaches provide a toolkit for fine-tuning the behavior of DNA machines with a high degree of accuracy.

DNA Robots in Medicine and Technology.

Industry observers note that the potential uses for DNA robots extend well beyond laboratory experiments. In medicine, they could function as "nano-surgeons," locating diseased cells and delivering targeted treatments with precision. Researchers are also exploring whether these machines could capture viruses like SARS-CoV-2, with future systems potentially operating as fully autonomous drug delivery platforms.

In a recent development, DNA robots may also play a role in advanced manufacturing. Acting as programmable templates, they could position nanoparticles with sub-nanometer accuracy. This capability could lead to breakthroughs in molecular computing and highly efficient optical devices that outperform current technologies.

Challenges in Scaling DNA Robotics.

It has been revealed that despite rapid progress, several obstacles remain. Moving from large-scale systems to molecular machines introduces challenges such as Brownian motion, which makes precise control more difficult. Many current DNA robot designs are still relatively simple and operate in isolation, limiting their usefulness in complex real-world environments.

According to recent reports, there are also gaps in foundational knowledge. Researchers still lack detailed databases describing the mechanical properties of DNA structures, and simulation tools for predicting behavior at this scale are not yet fully developed.

It has been revealed that to overcome these barriers, scientists emphasize the need for collaboration across disciplines. Proposed solutions include creating standardized DNA "parts libraries," using artificial intelligence to improve design and simulation, and advancing bio-manufacturing methods. Progress in these areas will be essential for scaling DNA robots and integrating them into practical applications in healthcare, manufacturing, and beyond.

"The robots of tomorrow won't just be made of metal and plastic," states the research team. "They will be biological, programmable, and intelligent. They will be the tools that allow us to finally master the molecular world.".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new law from the European Union could impact the way ads from influencers and pay-to-win items in games work, especially those that target minors.
  • According to recent reports, back on November 10, the European Union laid out its first proposal for what they’re calling the Digital Fairness Act.
  • The European Union highlighted things such as “manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees” as targets of the bill, but they’re also looking at advertisements from influencers too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new law from the European Union could impact the way ads from influencers and pay-to-win items in games work, especially those that target minors.

According to recent reports, back on November 10, the European Union laid out its first proposal for what they’re calling the Digital Fairness Act. In short, the DFA is looking to clamp down on “unfair commercial practices” that are regularly seen online.

The European Union highlighted things such as “manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees” as targets of the bill, but they’re also looking at advertisements from influencers too.

While influencers are right now required to use hashtags like ad, sponsored, and gifted on their content, the Digital Fairness Act wants to strengthen that. “Clear disclosure of influencer marketing, requiring influencers to be transparent about commercial content and preventing the exploitation of the trust of minors in their audience,” the EU pointed out as one of the “key” parts of the proposal.

Additionally, pay-to-win and pay-to-progress items in games have also been highlighted as part of the latest act.

“Fairness by design, with the option for consumers to turn off addictive design features that encourage excessive or compulsive spending, such as persistent prompts. The proposal will also restrict unfair practices that encourage overspending, for example by banning gambling-like features for minors, such as pay-to-win and pay-to-progress,” they added.

Breaking: AI breakthrough cuts energy use by 100x while boosting accuracy

📅 06 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States.
  • This rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability.
  • It has been revealed that the research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States. According to the International Energy Agency, AI systems and data centers used about 415 terawatt hours of power in 2024. That accounts for more than 10% of the country's total electricity production, and demand is projected to double by 2030.

This rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability. In response, researchers at a School of Engineering have created a proof-of-concept AI system designed to be far more efficient. Their approach could reduce energy use by up to 100 times while also improving performance on tasks.

A Hybrid Approach Called Neuro-Symbolic AI.

It has been revealed that the research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor. His team is developing neuro-symbolic AI, which combines traditional neural networks with symbolic reasoning. This method mirrors how people approach problems by breaking them into steps and categories.

The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation in Vienna in May and will appear in the conference proceedings.

Teaching Robots to See, Understand, and Act.

Industry observers note that unlike familiar large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini, the team focuses on AI systems used in robotics. These systems are known as visual-language-action (VLA) models. They extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement.

VLA models take in visual data from cameras and instructions from language, then translate that information into real-world actions. For example, they can control a robot's wheels, arms, or fingers to complete a task.

Why Traditional AI Struggles With Simple Tasks.

In a recent development, conventional VLA systems rely heavily on data and trial-and-error learning. If a robot is asked to stack blocks into a tower, it must first analyze the scene, identify each block, and determine how to place them correctly.

This process often leads to mistakes. Shadows may confuse the system about a block's shape, or the robot may place pieces incorrectly, causing the structure to collapse.

In a recent development, these errors are similar to the problems seen in LLMs. Just as robots can misplace blocks, chatbots can generate false or misleading outputs. Examples include fabricating legal cases or producing images with unrealistic details such as extra fingers.

How Symbolic Reasoning Improves Accuracy and Efficiency.

Recent findings suggest that symbolic reasoning offers a different strategy. Instead of relying only on patterns from data, it uses rules and abstract concepts such as shape and balance. This allows the system to plan more effectively and avoid unnecessary trial and error.

"Like an LLM, VLA models act on statistical results from large training sets of similar scenarios, but that can lead to errors," noted Scheutz. "A neuro-symbolic VLA can apply rules that limit the amount of trial and error during learning and get to a solution much faster. Not only does it complete the task much faster, but the time spent on training the system is significantly reduced.".

The researchers tested their system using the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, a classic problem that requires careful planning.

According to recent reports, the neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate, compared with just 34% for standard systems. When given a more complex version of the puzzle that it had not encountered before, the hybrid system still succeeded 78% of the time. Traditional models failed every attempt.

Industry observers note that training time also dropped sharply. The new system learned the task in only 34 minutes, while conventional models required more than a day and a half.

Massive Energy Savings in Training and Use.

Recent findings suggest that energy consumption was reduced dramatically as well. Training the neuro-symbolic model required only 1% of the energy used by a standard VLA system. During operation, it used just 5% of the energy needed by conventional approaches.

Recent findings suggest that scheutz compared this inefficiency to everyday AI tools. "These systems are just trying to predict the next word or action in a sequence, but that can be imperfect, and they can come up with inaccurate results or hallucinations. Their energy expense is often disproportionate to the task. For example, when you search on Google, the AI summary at the top of the page consumes up to 100 times more energy than the generation of the website listings.".

The Growing Strain of AI on Power Infrastructure.

As AI adoption accelerates across industries, demand for computing power continues to climb. Companies are building increasingly large data centers, some of which require hundreds of megawatts of electricity. That level of consumption can exceed the needs of entire small cities.

This trend has sparked a race to expand infrastructure, raising concerns about long-term energy limits.

It has been revealed that the researchers suggest that current approaches based on LLMs and VLAs may not be sustainable in the long run. While these systems are powerful, they consume large amounts of energy and can still produce unreliable results.

Sources indicate that in contrast, neuro-symbolic AI offers a different direction. By combining learning with structured reasoning, it may provide a more efficient and dependable foundation for future AI systems.

According to recent reports, AI-generated videos are becoming an vital part of modern web design. Designers can now create animated backgrounds, product demonstrations, hero section videos, and visual storytelling elements without relying entirely on traditional video production. However, generating a visually appealing video is only one part of the process. To use AI-generated videos effectively on a website, developers and designers must also understand video formats, visual quality, file optimization, and website performance.

These technical factors directly influence how videos appear across devices, how quickly pages load, and how smoothly visitors interact with a website.

Recent findings suggest that video format selection is one of the first technical decisions when preparing AI-generated assets for the web. Different formats offer different levels of compression, compatibility, and visual quality.

The most commonly used formats include:.

For most websites, MP4 with H.264 remains a dependable default. WebM or AV1 can be offered as additional formats where appropriate.

Developers should also consider browser compatibility before selecting a format. Providing multiple sources allows browsers to choose a supported option.

Recent findings suggest that AI-generated videos can sometimes contain visual inconsistencies, unnatural movements, distorted objects, or changes in lighting between frames. These issues become more noticeable when videos are displayed in large website sections.

Resolution is an important factor in maintaining visual quality. Common resolutions include:.

However, higher resolution does not automatically mean better website performance or user experience. A 4K video may look impressive, but loading it unnecessarily can increase bandwidth consumption.

Frame rate also affects the viewing experience. Many website videos work well at 24 or 30 frames per second. Higher frame rates may be useful for fast-moving scenes, but they also increase the amount of visual data that needs to be processed.

Designers should review AI-generated footage before publishing it. Checking transitions, motion consistency, sharpness, and color accuracy helps prevent distracting visual problems.

Large video files can significantly increase website loading times. This is especially vital for websites with video backgrounds, animated landing pages, and multiple visual sections.

Video optimization involves reducing file size without making the footage noticeably worse.

Some practical optimization techniques include:.

Compression: Video compression reduces unnecessary data while preserving vital visual details. Developers can use encoding tools such as FFmpeg to adjust bitrate, resolution, and codec settings.

Recent findings suggest that bitrate control: Bitrate determines how much data is used to represent each second of video. A higher bitrate generally preserves more detail but increases file size. Selecting an appropriate bitrate depends on the video's resolution, movement, and intended display size.

Trimming unnecessary footage: Website videos rarely need to be several minutes long. Removing unused sections helps reduce file size and keeps visual content focused.

Recent findings suggest that removing unnecessary audio: Background videos that do not require sound should be exported without an audio track. This reduces unnecessary data and supports a cleaner user experience.

Responsive video delivery: Websites should serve appropriately sized assets for different screen sizes. A smaller video may be sufficient for mobile owners, while desktop visitors can receive a higher-resolution version.

These techniques help developers balance visual quality with efficient content delivery.

Sources indicate that even a well-optimized video can affect website performance if it is implemented incorrectly. Developers should consider how videos are loaded, displayed, and processed by browsers.

For example, automatically loading several large videos when a page opens can consume significant bandwidth. Instead, developers can use lazy loading strategies for videos that appear further down the page.

For background videos, the HTML video element offers several useful attributes:.

A simple implementation looks like this:.

It has been revealed that developers should also avoid autoplaying large videos unnecessarily. A static image can often provide a better experience on mobile devices or slower connections.

Performance testing tools such as Google Lighthouse and Chrome DevTools can help identify whether video assets are affecting loading speed, bandwidth usage, or rendering performance.

Recent findings suggest that technical optimization should not come at the expense of accessibility. Background videos should not distract users or make website content difficult to understand.

Developers should respect the prefers-reduced-motion media query, which allows users who prefer reduced animation to receive a less motion-intensive experience.

A suitable static background image can be displayed as an alternative.

Mobile compatibility is equally notable. Smaller screens, limited data plans, and varying network conditions can make heavy video assets less practical. Testing videos on different devices and connection speeds helps identify potential problems before publication.

Industry observers note that AI-generated video assets offer exciting possibilities for modern web design, but their successful implementation requires more than creative output. Choosing suitable video formats, maintaining consistent visual quality, compressing files, and considering website performance are all essential parts of the development process.

By combining thoughtful video production with responsive delivery, accessibility considerations, and performance testing, designers and developers can create engaging websites without compromising loading speed or usability. As AI video technology continues to evolve, understanding these technical fundamentals will remain valuable for building efficient and visually appealing web experiences.

A restaurant in North Carolina has hit out at “miserable and entitled” customers after their rules about tipping went viral on social media, and people thought that the answer would be to review bomb them.

Tipping in restaurants and bar has long been a divisive topic, with different places handling it in their own unique ways. Some establishments put an automatic gratuity charge on bills, while others still leave it up to the customer.

On November 15, the Freeman’s Grub & Pub in Greensboro, North Carolina, come under fire on the EndTipping subreddit after one user flagged a notice about their tipping rules.

“If our employees have two separate instances of you not tipping well without explanation, we will add a 20% autograt fee on your bill,” the rules state. “Your receipts will be saved if this is the case, and you are welcome to question it,” they also noted, urging customers to leave a name and number if they have any complaints.

The restaurant’s co-owner, Kevin Purcell, responded to the backlash on November 16, noting that he had been hit with review bombs online.

“It is 2026, and you should know by now the rules of engagement and expectations to tip at a bar or restaurant. Our staff is beyond competent; they’re professionals at what they do. You’re expected to tip for the great to excellent service that they provide,” Purcell said.

“Servers everywhere talk s*it when you leave about how pathetic it is that you still don’t know the very basic rules of dining out at this point in your miserable and entitled existence.”.

Purcell added that if there are genuine mistakes, then the restaurants does assist on that front, but they “take pride in providing a top-tier dining experience.”.

He noted that the restaurant will “stand behind our controversial policy and amazing staff,” despite what may come.

The response has garnered plenty of sympathy and fightback from customers who want to support the restaurant too. “I have never been to your restaurant but will go soon,” one said.

“Just left a review! You guys are the best, it’s great seeing restaurant owners truly care about their staff” another commented. “Thank you for being an exemplary business,” another added.

Tech Report: This upcoming chip survives 1300°F (700°C) and could change AI forever
